registry_patch.wiki_article:
Monetary Dark Matter (EA-SE-DARK-01 v0.2) develops a relational account of what monetary representation can leave non-binding without making it causally irrelevant. Its central object is not a hidden quantity of money but a field of pre-existing relations that remain constitutively or causally load-bearing after monetary shear has removed their operative standing. The paper distinguishes constitutive labor, which makes and transmits the value-bearing field, from shear labor, which selects, resolves, commensurates, prices or settles that field. It then isolates productive provenance shear: the stronger case in which a monetary position gains capacity when a specific obligating relation ceases to bind even though the position continues to depend on the world that relation helped constitute.

The paper derives monetary shear through Marx's value-form analysis and uses the 1867 first-edition Form IV as an instrument for reading a monetary body capable of bearing a second magnitude not exhausted by denomination. Its inscribed-currency specimen is deliberately unresolved: reference, premium and absence of a claim are observed; the causal contribution of reference to the premium is inferred; and the stronger claim that non-binding status itself contributes positively to the premium remains untested pending matched controls.

Section 25 factors realized standing as activation times constitutive presence and rotates the synchronic theory toward deposit #1630's transition problem. Appendix A introduces a second, heterogeneous counter-transition on the monetary carrier. The final pre-deposit model separates circulating inscription-bearing carriers from cumulative effective exposure: carrier withdrawal can reduce future exposure generation without undoing exposure already acquired. The revision frontier remains open and names the empirical work required before the productive-shear claim can advance to a settled result.

defines_concepts.definition: The subset of relations excluded from operative monetary standing that remain constitutively or causally load-bearing for the monetary result or the capacities it enables.
The transformation by which an already constituted and transmissible semantic field is divided into what monetary grammar retains as operative and what it can cease to require.
A regime in which deactivating a specific obligating relation increases a monetary capacity or value while the resulting position continues to depend on the world that relation helped constitute.
Provenance relations whose activation can alter permission, distribution, attribution, ownership, liability, settlement, or recognized standing.
An audit object pairing a monetary scalar with the excluded-but-load-bearing relation field that monetary representation does not make binding; it is not a sum of hidden dollars.
A conditional negative feedback in which withdrawal of inscription-bearing monetary carriers reduces future exposure production without reversing cumulative exposure already acquired.
